MCA approved training providers (ATP)
How to find MCA approved training providers for STCW short course and ancillary training. This page is updated monthly.
- From:
- Maritime and Coastguard Agency
- Published:
- 11 July 2014
- Last updated:
- 5 November 2026 — See all updates
Approved nautical colleges
Other maritime administrations
The MCA accepts some STCW short courses from other maritime administrations. For more information, please see section 4 of MIN 643.
We do not accept any online courses where there is a requirement for face-to-face practical training in the STCW Code
STCW basic training:
- Personal Survival Techniques (PDF, 251 KB, 7 pages)
- Fire Prevention and Fire Fighting (PDF, 205 KB, 5 pages)
- Elementary First Aid (PDF, 276 KB, 8 pages)
- Personal Safety and Social Responsibility (PDF, 234 KB, 6 pages)
OneOcean is the MCA’s provider for the online ‘Prevention and Response to Violence & Harassment’ module referenced in MGN 718.

- Non-STCW Small Ships Navigation & Radar Training (under WBC3 syllabus) (PDF, 131 KB, 3 pages)
- Non-STCW One Day Stability Course (under WBC3 syllabus) (PDF, 134 KB, 3 pages)

- Generic MASS Remote Operator Training Course (under MGN 703) (PDF, 107 KB, 2 pages)
- Large Yacht Helideck Safety Training (PDF, 96.5 KB, 2 pages)
Boat Master Licence
Training provider not listed
1). Does the training provider state the course is MCA approved?
If not, it is unlikely to be approved by the MCA. You should instead find out which administration approved this (by checking the course web page or by contacting the training provider) and check whether we can accept/recognise the course.
2). Could the company you found be acting as an intermediary?
The company advertising MCA approved courses may not be the provider delivering the training but are instead acting as a commercial partner. In most cases, the course web page will tell you who the actual training provider is.
